This paper investigates the expressive power of Constraint Handling Languages (CHR) when the number of atoms in rule heads is restricted. We demonstrate that the resulting language is decidable if the number of atoms is bounded by a constant, whereas it becomes undecidable when the number of atoms is unbounded.

This study investigates the galaxy spin direction dipole axis within the 100 Mpc region surrounding the Milky Way, utilizing data from the 2MASS Redshift Survey (2MRS) and the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS). We examine the alignment of these dipole axes with the Milky Way's spin axis and the local galaxy distribution. Our findings indicate that the dipole axes derived from both 2MRS and SDSS are nearly parallel to the Milky Way's spin axis, with a separation angle of approximately 20 degrees. Furthermore, the dipole axes from both surveys align closely with the local galaxy distribution, showing an angular difference of roughly 10 degrees. These results suggest that the local galaxy distribution is not merely a random fluctuation but is instead influenced by the Milky Way's spin axis.

Few-shot learning (FSL) has garnered significant interest due to its ability to learn from limited labeled data. While recent FSL approaches have demonstrated strong performance, they often rely on sampling techniques that are computationally expensive and fail to account for label noise. To address these limitations, we introduce Eigen-Reptile, a novel method that integrates the Eigen-Covariance metric with the Reptile algorithm. By leveraging the Eigen-Covariance metric, Eigen-Reptile effectively captures the intrinsic structure of the feature space, thereby enhancing the model's generalization capabilities. Furthermore, the method employs a new sampling strategy that significantly reduces computational costs while mitigating the impact of label noise. Empirical evaluations across multiple benchmarks confirm that Eigen-Reptile outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods.

This study introduces a novel framework for predicting cognitive decline in Alzheimer's disease (AD) by integrating MRI data with Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) scores. The proposed method utilizes a deep learning architecture that fuses a 3D convolutional neural network (CNN) for MRI analysis with a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network for MMSE processing. The system is trained to forecast the MMSE score of a patient's next visit based on their current MRI and MMSE data. The model was evaluated using a dataset comprising 1,000 patients from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) with a 12-month follow-up period. Results indicate that the proposed approach outperforms baseline methods, achieving a mean absolute error of 0.83 and a mean squared error of 1.69.

The field of AI Ethics has recently gained significant traction, yet the specific methodologies for conducting ethical analysis remain undefined. This study examines the literature on AI Ethics to determine the optimal approach for ethical evaluation. We propose that such analysis should be conducted through a multi-perspective framework, where the viewpoints of all stakeholders involved are considered. Furthermore, we argue that ethical analysis must be integrated with technical analysis, as the two are deeply interconnected.

This paper investigates the decidability of properties concerning word languages over infinite words, specifically within the framework of the Boolean-closed full trios. We demonstrate that the ω-regular languages constitute the unique such trio that is decidable. Furthermore, we establish that determining whether a given ω-regular language belongs to a specific Boolean-closed full trio is undecidable.

This study introduces a hybrid channel estimation framework that combines a deep neural network (DNN) with a least squares (LS) algorithm. The DNN component forecasts the channel state for the current time slot by leveraging the LS estimate from the immediately preceding slot and the channel state from two slots back. The proposed method is evaluated against both the LS algorithm and a conventional hybrid scheme that utilizes the LS estimate from the previous slot alongside the channel state from two slots back. The results demonstrate that the new hybrid approach achieves superior accuracy compared to the traditional hybrid method, while also outperforming the standard LS algorithm.

Recent discrepancies between Standard Model predictions and experimental data for $V_{ud}$ and $V_{us}$ hint at physics beyond the Standard Model. This study examines the impact of a new scalar leptoquark on these anomalies, specifically within the framework of the minimal flavor violation (MFV) paradigm. We demonstrate that a scalar leptoquark with a mass around 1 TeV can resolve the $V_{ud}$ anomaly, whereas a leptoquark of approximately 10 TeV is required to address the $V_{us}$ anomaly. Furthermore, we analyze the implications of these scenarios for the unitarity of the CKM matrix and the flavor-changing neutral current process $b \to s \gamma$.

This study introduces a novel approach to image segmentation that leverages dilated kernels within convolution layers to enhance receptive fields. By employing these dilated kernels, the network can effectively capture contextual information across various scales, thereby improving its ability to distinguish between different semantic classes. The proposed architecture is built upon a U-Net framework, which integrates skip connections to facilitate the flow of both low-level and high-level features. The network is trained using a combination of Dice loss and cross-entropy loss. The authors evaluated the model on the ISIC 2017 dataset, demonstrating that it achieves superior performance compared to several existing state-of-the-art methods.

This paper introduces a novel approach to data view semantics that utilizes a specific type of dependency to isolate private data from shared data. We demonstrate that this approach is equivalent to one based on a distinct semantic framework relying on the concept of view independence.

This study investigates the characteristics of hot dust emission in galaxies, utilizing data from the Herschel Space Observatory. We analyzed 1,000 galaxies from the Herschel Reference Survey (HRS), which were selected based on their radio luminosity ($L_{\rm 1.4\,GHz}$) and morphological classification. The sample includes 1,000 galaxies with $L_{\rm 1.4\,GHz}$ values ranging from $10^{9}$ to $10^{11}$ W Hz$^{-1}$, covering both spiral and irregular types. We measured the flux density at 160 $\mu$m and derived the corresponding dust temperature ($T_{\rm dust}$) and mass ($M_{\rm dust}$) for each source. Our findings indicate that galaxies with higher radio luminosity exhibit stronger hot dust emission, a trend that is more pronounced in irregular galaxies than in spirals. Furthermore, we observed a correlation between the dust temperature and the dust-to-gas ratio, as well as a link between dust mass and the dust-to-gas ratio. These results suggest that hot dust emission is a reliable tracer for the dust-to-gas ratio, particularly in irregular galaxies.

This paper introduces the MORALCOT prompting strategy, designed to enhance AI systems' grasp of human moral reasoning. By leveraging Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting, MORALCOT guides models to emulate the step-by-step logic humans employ when making ethical decisions. We demonstrate that this approach significantly boosts performance on the Moral Judgment Benchmark (MJB) compared to standard CoT methods. Furthermore, we analyze the impact of various factors on the system's ability to mimic human moral judgment, including the number of reasoning steps, the specific types of reasoning employed, and the selection of training data.

This note demonstrates that a valuation ring whose residue field has characteristic $p$ can be expressed as the direct limit of complete intersection valuation rings, each possessing a complete intersection residue ring with characteristic $p$.
This paper provides a concise overview of the Dirac equation in two dimensions, highlighting its contemporary applications and offering a systematic derivation of its solutions.

Model Predictive Control (MPC) has become a standard approach for solving complex control challenges in cooperative driving. By leveraging the ability to incorporate constraints and handle multi-agent interactions, MPC excels in these scenarios. However, its computational demands often hinder real-time implementation. This paper introduces a novel MPC framework designed for cooperative driving that utilizes a hybrid architecture combining deep neural networks with a traditional MPC solver. The proposed method relies on a pre-trained neural network to forecast the trajectories of surrounding vehicles, thereby reducing the number of variables within the optimization problem. Additionally, the study evaluates the method's performance in a multi-vehicle context and compares it against conventional MPC techniques.

The rapid expansion of social media has significantly altered how individuals access and share information. While this accessibility empowers users to disseminate their views, it also fosters a tendency to prioritize content that aligns with existing beliefs, often disregarding opposing perspectives. This phenomenon, known as echo chambers, reinforces pre-existing opinions and can lead to the rejection of credible information. To counteract this, we propose a novel approach that leverages social media to enhance the visibility of trustworthy content. Our method utilizes a graph-based model to identify and highlight information that is both credible and relevant to a user's specific interests. We validate this approach through a case study involving the COVID-19 pandemic, demonstrating its effectiveness in surfacing pertinent and reliable data.

This paper introduces $\pi$-ROAD, a novel framework designed to assist road operators in managing network resources during emergencies. The system leverages data from IoT sensors and video cameras to detect incidents and automatically generate alerts. It also provides a dashboard for operators to monitor the status of road sections and receive notifications regarding specific events.

This study introduces a collaborative framework for a dual-robot system designed to transport a shared object. The proposed method integrates a specific motion planning algorithm with a control strategy to ensure the robots navigate together while avoiding collisions. To achieve this, the Artificial Potential Fields (APF) algorithm is employed for collision avoidance, which, however, can induce path oscillations. To mitigate these oscillations, the paper proposes a control strategy that utilizes the robots' velocity and acceleration as inputs. The efficacy of this approach is validated through simulations involving two robots carrying a shared object.

The rise in machine intelligence and autonomous systems is fundamentally reshaping urban environments, creating a new landscape where cities are increasingly managed by algorithms. This shift is altering the very essence of urban living, as the integration of autonomous vehicles and smart technologies is redefining how individuals interact with their surroundings. This paper examines the profound implications of this transition, exploring how algorithmic governance is transforming the social, economic, and political fabric of our society.

This paper investigates online caching with side information, where a server predicts the future request sequence. We introduce a novel competitive analysis framework that evaluates the server's performance against an optimal offline algorithm, accounting for the prediction error. Our approach yields a competitive ratio of $O(\log k)$, where $k$ represents the cache size, provided that the prediction error remains within $O(k)$. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this result is optimal by establishing a lower bound of $\Omega(\log k)$.

The Trilateral Attention Network (TrA-Net) is a pioneering architecture designed for image segmentation, featuring three distinct pathways that capture complementary features. While these pathways enhance performance, their specific contributions remain unclear. This study introduces a novel method to quantify the importance of TrA-Net's pathways by leveraging the concept of information gain. We propose a new metric, the Information Gain Score (IGS), which evaluates pathway significance by measuring the information loss in segmentation outcomes when a pathway is removed. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach effectively quantifies pathway importance and offers valuable insights into the TrA-Net's internal mechanisms.
This study examines the linearized supergeometry of superspace, specifically focusing on how gauge fields for the super-Minkowski manifold are determined by torsion constraints.

This paper introduces a method for evaluating the quality of training data in machine learning by analyzing the impact of individual examples on model performance. By examining how specific data points influence the learning process, we can determine their relative importance and use this insight to assess the quality of the underlying dataset.

We demonstrate that the non-abelian matrix Berry phase arising from the entanglement of edge states within the quantum Hall effect drives charge pumping in the Hall surface. This phenomenon is described by a non-abelian Chern-Simons theory, which is derived from a non-abelian bulk-boundary correspondence.

We introduce METRO-LM, a series of large language models designed to deliver state-of-the-art performance on various benchmarks while maintaining high efficiency. These models are trained using a novel curriculum that prioritizes the most informative data, enabling them to outperform earlier large models on multiple tasks despite using significantly fewer parameters. The models are available in sizes ranging from 125M to 1.5B parameters.

This study introduces a method for inferring the topology of quantum networks using only local measurements. We demonstrate that the network's adjacency matrix can be reconstructed from local density matrices, which are derived from measurements performed on individual nodes. The proposed approach is validated through numerical simulations on various network configurations, including star, line, and complete graphs.

This study investigates how different introduction strategies influence the ability to explain visual encodings to an audience. We conducted a user study involving 100 participants to assess the effectiveness of four distinct approaches: (1) a standard explanation, (2) a visual explanation, (3) a visual explanation with a "before" state, and (4) a visual explanation with a "before and after" comparison. The results indicate that the "before and after" strategy is the most effective, followed by the "before" approach, the standard explanation, and finally the visual explanation alone.

We examine the impact of Floquet heating on the quantum control of many-body systems via optical means. Our analysis demonstrates that this heating can be advantageous, as it suppresses order within the Floquet spectrum, thereby enhancing the stability of quantum states against heating effects.

Counterfactual planning involves generating hypothetical scenarios to evaluate the consequences of specific actions. This paper introduces a novel method for creating counterfactuals that explicitly accounts for uncertainty regarding model parameters. By integrating this uncertainty, the resulting plans become more robust and resilient to variations in the environment. We demonstrate the efficacy of our approach through experiments in a stochastic grid-world setting, where we assess the quality of plans derived from both deterministic and stochastic models.

This study introduces a new approach to urban sound classification that leverages the complementary strengths of both convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs). The proposed architecture utilizes a CNN to extract features from spectrograms, which are then processed by an RNN to capture temporal dependencies. Experimental evaluations on the ESC-50 and US8k datasets achieved accuracies of 89.1% and 93.1%, respectively. These results surpass the performance of existing state-of-the-art models, including those based on CNNs, RNNs, and hybrid architectures.

We examine $N=4$ $SO(8)$ gauged supergravity within the context of $AdS_4$ black holes, specifically focusing on those possessing $SO(2)\times SO(2)$ isometry. This framework encompasses both the $SO(4)\times SO(4)$ symmetric Reissner-Nordström black hole and the $SO(3)\times SO(3)$ dyonic black hole. Our analysis demonstrates that both the $AdS_2\times S^2$ and $AdS_2\times H^2$ geometries emerge as solutions for the $SO(4)\times SO(4)$ black hole, whereas the $SO(3)\times SO(3)$ solution admits only the $AdS_2\times S^2$ geometry. Furthermore, we derive the corresponding near-horizon limits for these configurations.

This paper introduces SCAMP-5, a new compiler designed for the SCAMP language, which serves as a high-level abstraction for quantum computing. The compiler translates SCAMP code into QASM, which is subsequently executed on the IBM Quantum Experience platform. We have also developed Cain, a specialized compiler that compiles SCAMP code directly into QASM, bypassing the need for an intermediate compiler. Our analysis reveals that Cain produces significantly more compact QASM code compared to SCAMP-5. Furthermore, we demonstrate that Cain can generate QASM code that is shorter than that produced by IBM's native compiler.

This study examines the generalized Witten effect within the framework of quantum gravity, specifically focusing on how quantum corrections influence the spectrum of charged states. We demonstrate that this effect can be expressed through the prepotential of the vector multiplet moduli space, which is determined by the Seiberg-Witten curve. Furthermore, we analyze the generalized Witten effect in the context of M-theory compactified on a K3 surface.

We introduce two new variations of regret pruning, a technique designed to learn Nash equilibria in extensive-form games. Unlike the original method, which relies on a single regret update per information set per iteration, our proposed variations incorporate multiple updates per information set per iteration. We demonstrate that these approaches offer superior performance compared to the single-update baseline.

This paper presents a novel modal logic grounded in the semantics of possible states-of-affairs, designed to expand the scope of Aristotle's modal syllogistic. By doing so, it offers a more comprehensive understanding of Aristotelian syllogistic reasoning and provides a framework for developing modal syllogistic systems for other logical traditions.

Causal inequalities serve as a tool to determine whether a specific causal order exists between two events. While classical causal inequalities can be violated with detectors operating at any non-zero efficiency, quantum causal inequalities demand a minimum efficiency threshold to achieve violation. This study examines the relationship between these two types of inequalities within a framework of causally disconnected events. We demonstrate that a violation of a classical causal inequality by quantum correlations necessarily entails a violation of a corresponding quantum causal inequality. Furthermore, we show that the maximum violation achievable by quantum causal inequalities is bounded by the violation observed in classical causal inequalities.

This study introduces a dual-critic reinforcement learning framework designed to optimize video encoding by jointly managing distortion and rate constraints. The method employs two separate critic networks to evaluate the expected cumulative costs associated with each objective, while a single actor network generates encoding decisions. To address the high variance inherent in reinforcement learning, we implement a variance reduction technique that leverages the correlation between the two critic networks. Experimental results indicate that this approach surpasses both traditional rate-distortion optimization methods and existing RL-based encoders in terms of rate-distortion performance.

This study investigates the gas-phase chemistry of carbon and oxygen in protoplanetary disks, specifically examining how the photo-ablation of carbon-rich grains sustains a long-lived chemical equilibrium. We developed a comprehensive chemical network incorporating 100 species and 1,000 reactions, which accounts for the photo-ablation of carbonaceous grains and the subsequent formation of CO. Our findings indicate that this ablation process is essential for maintaining a prolonged equilibrium cycle, particularly in the outer disk regions. Additionally, we analyzed the impact of varying carbonaceous grain properties on the chemical composition, revealing that while the abundance of CO remains largely insensitive to grain characteristics, the abundances of other carbon-bearing species are significantly affected.

We introduce NeuralCut, a novel framework for selecting cuts in mixed-integer linear programming (MILP). This approach utilizes a neural network to identify the most effective cuts for a given problem, surpassing existing baselines by generating cuts that are both more potent and more diverse. The model's efficacy is demonstrated through its ability to solve MILP instances from the MIPLIB 2010 benchmark that were previously intractable for state-of-the-art solvers.

This study examines the superconducting properties of T$_d$-Mo$_{1-x}$Ir$_{x}$Te$_{2}$, a material that exhibits a transition from nodal-line superconductivity to fully gapped superconductivity as the iridium concentration ($x$) increases. The superconducting gap is found to be highly anisotropic, with its magnitude varying significantly across different directions. Furthermore, the superconducting critical temperature ($T_c$) displays a pronounced dependence on the magnetic field orientation, a behavior attributed to the material's anisotropic gap structure.

This study examines the application of Natural Language Processing (NLP) methods to enhance the retrieval of duplicate bug reports. We introduce a novel dataset comprising 1,000 pairs of identical bug reports, which we utilize to evaluate various retrieval strategies. Our findings indicate that incorporating NLP techniques significantly boosts the effectiveness of the retrieval process.

We introduce a strongly coupled effective field theory that captures the essential characteristics of the graphene phase transition. This framework elucidates the non-perturbative renormalization group flow of the theory's couplings, thereby clarifying the critical behavior observed in the transition.

This study introduces a self-supervised teacher-student framework designed to enhance Named Entity Recognition (NER) performance. The proposed method leverages a teacher-student architecture to generate pseudo-labels for unlabeled data, which are subsequently utilized to train the student model. The teacher model is refined through an ensemble of three distinct training strategies: (1) a standard training approach, (2) a self-training mechanism, and (3) a data augmentation technique. The results demonstrate that this framework significantly boosts the performance of the BiLSTM-CRF model, achieving F1-scores of 89.1% and 89.2% on the CoNLL-2003 and CoNLL-2004 datasets, respectively.

Social media platforms like Twitter and Instagram have become essential for individuals to share travel experiences and seek recommendations. Consequently, the tourism sector has begun leveraging this user-generated content to gain valuable insights into traveler preferences and behaviors. This study introduces a novel approach for automatically extracting and categorizing travel-related topics from Twitter data. We developed a specialized dataset comprising 10,000 tweets, which was used to train a BERT-based model. The system successfully identifies 10 distinct categories of tourism-related subjects. Furthermore, we evaluated the model's performance using a separate test set of 1,000 tweets, demonstrating its effectiveness. The research concludes that this methodology offers a robust solution for automatically detecting tourism-related themes within social media data.

This study introduces a machine learning framework designed to predict the effective properties of microstructured materials. The method utilizes a graph neural network (GNN) to forecast the effective elastic tensor of two-dimensional linear elastic materials based on their microstructure. The network is trained on a dataset comprising 10,000 GNNs, each representing a two-dimensional microstructure with randomly distributed inclusions. The model's performance is evaluated against analytical solutions for specific cases, including square and triangular arrangements of inclusions, as well as numerical solutions derived from the finite element method. The results demonstrate that the proposed GNN achieves high accuracy in predicting effective elastic properties.

This study presents the inaugural detection of a disk gap in the protoplanetary disk surrounding the young star CI Tau, utilizing the 30-meter class Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) via the SPHERE instrument. The gap was identified through angular differential imaging (ADI) at a 0.02 arcsecond separation, with a contrast sensitivity of 10^-4.1. The gap's location aligns with the predicted orbital radius of the planet CI Tau b, which has a mass of 1.5 Jupiter masses. The planet's migration is ruled out as the cause of the gap because the observed contrast at the gap's position exceeds the detection threshold for a gap-free disk. This study examines the correspondence between finite-energy free motion on a sphere and zero-energy trajectories within a specific potential. We demonstrate that the Kepler problem in this framework is equivalent to geodesics on a sphere, and we extend this finding to the Kepler problem in the context of the hydrogen atom.

This study examines the presence of non-trivial solutions for the non-local integro-differential equation
$$
\begin{cases}
(-\Delta)^s_{\mathfrak{g}}u = \lambda u + f(u) & \text{in } \Omega, \\
u = 0 & \text{in } \Omega^c,
\end{cases}
$$
where $\Omega$ is a bounded domain within a complete Riemannian manifold $(\mathfrak{g}, \mathfrak{d})$, $\lambda$ is a real parameter, and $f$ is a superlinear function. The operator $(-\Delta)^s_{\mathfrak{g}}$ represents a non-local, fractional Laplacian defined on $\mathfrak{g}$ with a singular exponent $s \in (0,1)$. We establish the existence of solutions by applying a mountain pass theorem, under the assumption that the manifold $\mathfrak{g}$ possesses a specific geometric structure.

This paper introduces a new approach to unlabelled multi-object filtering that utilizes a Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) method to estimate the posterior distribution of object trajectories. By employing a particle-based representation for the object posterior, the proposed method enhances trajectory estimation capabilities. The framework is designed to handle various multi-object scenarios, including detection, tracking, and data association. The object posterior is modeled as a mixture of trajectories, where each trajectory is represented by a set of particles. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through simulations involving a linear motion model and a linear-Gaussian measurement model.

This study introduces a novel stability assessment criterion for large-scale power systems featuring high levels of power converter integration. The proposed approach utilizes a reduced-order model of the power system, which is derived by applying the singular perturbation method to a comprehensive full-order model. The resulting stability assessment criterion is formulated based on the eigenvalues of this reduced-order model. The paper further demonstrates that this new criterion is more effective than traditional methods for evaluating the stability of extensive power systems with significant converter penetration.

This study introduces a novel approach to signature forgery detection that leverages the distinctiveness, complexity, and repeatables of signature templates. The method utilizes a deep learning framework to extract features from the three modalities, which are then fused to train a classifier for detection purposes. Experimental results demonstrate that this proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques.
We demonstrate that Hardy sums can be understood as enumerating oriented geodesics, thereby providing a geometric perspective on Dirichlet series associated with the Hardy sums.

The increasing popularity of mobile devices has driven the creation of numerous applications, with many now offering personalized experiences based on user preferences. However, the sheer volume of available apps makes it difficult for users to identify which ones best suit their specific needs. This paper introduces a recommendation system designed to suggest mobile applications by leveraging persistent contextual values. These long-term context elements, such as user demographics and interests, are utilized to customize the app discovery process. The system employs a hybrid recommendation approach that integrates both collaborative filtering and content-based techniques. It utilizes a user-item matrix to calculate similarity scores between users and items, while also incorporating content-based features to assess the relevance of apps to individual users. The proposed model was evaluated using the Google Play Store dataset, with performance measured through Mean Average Precision (MAP) and Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain (NDCG). Results indicate that the hybrid model outperforms standalone collaborative or content-based systems, achieving a MAP of 0.113 and an NDCG of 0.213.

This paper introduces a novel architecture designed for real-time monocular 6-DoF pose estimation. By leveraging a multi-scale feature pyramid, the model achieves high accuracy while maintaining computational efficiency. The system operates at 30 frames per second, delivering 6-DoF pose predictions with an average 6D error of 1.14 degrees and 1.2 pixels.

This study presents the inaugural flux calibration results from the 1.5-meter collimated instrument aboard AstroSat, India's first dedicated multi-wavelength astronomy satellite. The instrument, known as the Large Area X-ray Telescope (LAXRT), operates within the 2–100 keV energy range. This paper introduces a novel framework for categorizing blockchain protocols, distinguishing between permissioned and permissionless systems based on the specific roles of their participants. It outlines a methodology for classifying protocols according to their consensus mechanisms and explores the implications of these classifications for the design of permissioned blockchains.

This study employs an enhanced chromomagnetic interaction model to analyze the mass spectra of the $c\bar{c}q\bar{q}$ and $c\bar{c}q\bar{q}'$ tetraquark states. This study examines the impact of new physics on the Higgs mass bound derived from vacuum stability within the Standard Model. We demonstrate that when the scale of instability is raised by new physics, the resulting constraints on the Higgs mass are significantly relaxed. Furthermore, we analyze the implications of this mechanism for the Higgs mass in the context of the Standard Model augmented by a real singlet scalar.
This paper investigates the connection between the $p$-Hamilton-Jacobi equation and the $\sigma$-Talagrand inequality within Carnot groups.

This study introduces a new estimator termed the exponentially weighted divergence (EWD) estimator, which is derived from an exponentially weighted version of the density power divergence (DPD) estimator. We demonstrate that the EWD estimator retains the robustness and efficiency characteristics of the DPD estimator. Furthermore, we establish the consistency and asymptotic normality of the EWD estimator. Through a simulation study, we evaluate the performance of the EWD estimator against the DPD estimator, as well as the maximum likelihood and minimum density power divergence estimators, specifically under conditions of data contamination.

This paper introduces a novel algorithm designed to enhance image quality by leveraging the distinct characteristics of static and motion-focused pixels. The method employs a two-stage process: initially, it identifies and classifies pixels as either static or dynamic, followed by a second stage that selectively applies restoration techniques exclusively to the dynamic regions. The proposed algorithm is evaluated against various existing methods, demonstrating its superior performance.

This study examines the variance of coefficients in the characteristic polynomial of a random directed graph, where edges are selected independently with a fixed probability $p$. We demonstrate that for any fixed $p$, the variance of coefficients corresponding to periodic orbits containing self-intersections remains bounded, whereas the variance for those without self-intersections increases without limit. This finding indicates that the probability of self-intersections occurring in periodic orbits is negligible.

The analysis focuses on 1,000,000 stars with periods between 0.1 and 100 days, selected from the Gaia Variable Star Catalog (GVC). This paper investigates the classification of linear time-invariant systems as negative imaginary (n.n.i.) or non-negative imaginary (nni). It is demonstrated that the closest n.n.i. system to a given one can be derived from its non-n.n.i. counterpart by removing the non-n.n.i. component. Furthermore, the study establishes that the proximity between two n.n.i. systems is measured by the norm of their difference, and the distance from an n.n.i. system to the set of all n.n.i. systems equals the norm of its non-n.n.i. component.

This study investigates continual learning within End-to-End Automatic Speech Recognition (E2E-ASR) by training a single model sequentially on multiple tasks. We evaluate three approaches: a standard baseline using fine-tuning, a method employing a single shared encoder with task-specific decoders, and a third utilizing a shared encoder combined with a task-specific adapter. Results indicate that the optimal continual learning strategy outperforms traditional fine-tuning by up to 10% on new tasks and achieves a 20% improvement on average across all tasks. Furthermore, the adapter-based method offers a cost-effective solution, delivering performance comparable to the best continual learning technique while requiring 20% fewer parameters.

Code-switching, the practice of mixing two or more languages within a single utterance, is prevalent in social media communications. This phenomenon presents significant challenges for sentiment analysis, particularly when dealing with code-switched text. This paper introduces a novel approach to sentiment analysis of code-switched text by leveraging the contextual information provided by pre-trained language models. The proposed method utilizes a multi-task learning framework to jointly train a model for both language identification and sentiment analysis. The study evaluates this approach on a newly developed dataset of code-switched text from Twitter, which consists of 1,000 English-Hindi mixed messages. The results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques for this task.

This study examines the three-loop seesaw model, which incorporates a scalar triplet and two right-handed neutrinos to generate small neutrino masses. We demonstrate that this framework can simultaneously account for the observed neutrino mass spectrum and the anomalous magnetic moment of the muon. Furthermore, we analyze the model's phenomenological implications, including its predictions for a scalar particle with mass below 129 GeV, the muon's electric dipole moment, and the muon anomalous magnetic moment.

This study introduces a novel Product-based Neural Network (PNN) designed to handle categorical data, leveraging a specific architecture to capture interactions between fields. The model employs a two-layer neural network where the first layer computes pairwise products of categorical values, and the second layer aggregates these interactions to generate a comprehensive representation. We demonstrate that this architecture can be interpreted as a two-layer neural network with a specific type of nonlinearity. Furthermore, we show that the PNN can be extended to handle multiple categorical values within a single field. The paper also outlines a method for estimating the PNN's parameters and provides an analysis of its asymptotic properties.

This study examines active beamforming design for an intelligent reflecting surface (IRS)-assisted network, accounting for channel state information (CSI) uncertainty. We formulate a robust optimization problem aimed at maximizing the minimum signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) across all users. To address the resulting non-convexity, we employ a block coordinate descent (BCD) algorithm that iteratively optimizes the transmit beamforming vectors and IRS phase shifts. Specifically, we resolve the transmit beamforming subproblem by leveraging semidefinite relaxation (SDR) and the S-Procedure, while the IRS phase shift subproblem is solved using a low-complexity alternating optimization approach. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing benchmarks in terms of robustness against CSI uncertainty and computational efficiency.

Branch prediction is a critical component of modern processors, and while traditional methods have long been the standard, dynamic predictors leveraging deep learning are increasingly gaining traction. This paper introduces a novel dynamic predictor that integrates a deep neural network with a 2-bit saturating counter. This hybrid approach combines the strengths of both deep learning and conventional techniques, resulting in superior performance compared to standalone dynamic predictors.

This paper introduces a deep convolutional neural network designed to autonomously manage a camera, track targets, and generate a comprehensive bird's-eye view of the environment. The system's efficacy is validated through a series of experiments conducted in both indoor and outdoor settings. The results demonstrate that this approach surpasses traditional methods in terms of accuracy, efficiency, and robustness.

This paper investigates the SOS model on a half-line with a boundary condition at the origin. We demonstrate the existence of non-normalizable boundary laws and establish that the model exhibits a phase transition.

This study introduces a theoretical framework for entangled two-photon resonance energy transfer (E2P) between two chromophores, driven by a single laser pulse. The model is derived from a microscopic description of the interaction between the laser and the two-photon system, utilizing a density matrix formalism to characterize the process. The analysis demonstrates that the E2P rate coefficient, $K_{E2P}$, can be expressed as a product of the two-photon absorption cross-section and the Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) rate. Furthermore, the paper derives an analytical formula for $K_{E2P}$, which is validated through numerical simulations. These simulations reveal that the E2P rate coefficient is highly sensitive to the detuning between the laser frequency and the two-photon resonance frequency.

This study examines the strong coupling constants for the $B_c$ meson decaying into $B$ or $D$ mesons alongside a $J/\psi$ or $\psi(2S)$ vector meson. The analysis utilizes the light-cone QCD sum rule framework, incorporating the leading-twist light-cone distribution amplitudes for the $B$ and $D$ mesons. The resulting coupling constants are compared against predictions from perturbative QCD and the non-relativistic QCD (NRQCD) formalism. The findings indicate that the strong coupling constants derived from light-cone QCD sum rules align more closely with those predicted by the NRQCD approach than with those from perturbative QCD.

This study examines the short-baseline neutrino oscillation anomalies by analyzing recent data from the MicroBooNE experiment, which was designed to investigate the anomalous electron neutrino appearance reported by the MiniBooNE collaboration. We present a comprehensive analysis of MicroBooNE's 2017 and 2018 data, covering both the near and far detector sites. Our findings indicate that the MicroBooNE results are consistent with the MiniBooNE anomalies, suggesting that the observed excess in the far detector can be explained by the same underlying physics. Furthermore, we explore the implications of these results for the sterile neutrino hypothesis and other new physics models.

This paper introduces a novel framework for designing observational studies that leverages the implicit weights generated by linear regression techniques, such as propensity score matching, regression adjustment, and IPTW. By conceptualizing these methods as linear regression models where the regressor is the propensity score, we demonstrate that the implicit weights function as a weighted average of treatment effects, with weights determined by the covariate distribution within the support of the propensity score. Consequently, this approach enables the derivation of design principles for observational studies and facilitates the construction of propensity score models that yield balanced covariate distributions and precise estimates of average treatment effects.

This study examines the impact of voltage source converters (VSCs) on grid-connected power system oscillations. It demonstrates that VSCs can effectively suppress oscillations by adjusting the active power output of synchronous generators. The paper derives a simplified model of the VSC, which is integrated into a linearized swing equation for synchronous machines. The analysis reveals that VSCs can regulate oscillations by modifying the damping coefficient of the swing equation. Furthermore, the work proposes a control strategy for VSCs that leverages the swing equation to enhance the damping of inter-area oscillations. The effectiveness of this approach is validated through simulations on a two-machine, one-area system.

We introduce a theoretical framework for analyzing the collective decay of two atoms within a cavity, accounting for the influence of a surrounding atomic cloud. This model accounts for the non-Markovian nature of the collective decay process, which arises from the finite size of the atomic ensemble. We demonstrate that the light emitted by the two-atom system displays non-classical characteristics, specifically sub-Poissonian statistics and photon antibunching. Furthermore, we show that the atomic cloud can induce non-Markovian dynamics in the two-atom system, which in turn enhances the non-classical features of the emitted light.

This study examines the stability of kinks within the $\phi^6$ model, which possesses internal modes. We demonstrate that internal modes can destabilize kinks, and we derive a stability criterion for such kinks. Furthermore, we analyze the influence of internal modes on the kink-antikink scattering process.

Generalized parton distributions (GPDs) are essential for comprehensively understanding hadron-production mechanisms and high-energy scattering. This study examines the evolution of GPDs within the leading-order DGLAP framework, specifically focusing on the $q \to qg$ splitting function. We derive a closed-form expression for this function and analyze its behavior across various scales. Furthermore, we investigate the connection between this splitting function and the hadronic matrix element of the twist-2 quark-gluon operator.

This study investigates the impact of discrete noise on text classification, specifically examining how it influences the decision boundaries of trained models. We introduce a novel approach to generate discrete noise by randomly substituting words within a document with a synonym selected from WordNet. Our findings indicate that this noise injection method effectively expands the model's decision boundaries, thereby enhancing generalization. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the proposed noise is highly effective for data augmentation, yielding performance improvements comparable to those achieved by existing data augmentation techniques.

This study introduces a novel approach to polyp detection in endoscopic videos by leveraging channel-aware attention mechanisms. We propose a new architecture that integrates a video encoder with a dedicated polyp detector. The encoder utilizes a channel-aware attention module to aggregate features across both spatial and temporal dimensions, while the detector employs a multi-scale fusion strategy to identify polyps. Experimental results on the public EndoVis 2017 dataset demonstrate that our method surpasses existing state-of-the-art techniques, achieving a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 84.0%.

This paper introduces a sequential sampling approach that allows for the regulation of spreading intensity, which can be adjusted at each step. The method is demonstrated through an application to the Metropolis-Hastings algorithm.

This paper examines the flat part of the moduli space of principally polarized abelian surfaces, specifically detailing its irreducible components. We demonstrate that these components correspond to torsion cosets within the moduli space of abelian surfaces, noting that each flat part component can be characterized as a collection of such cosets. Furthermore, we establish that the irreducible components of the minimal boundary of the moduli space of stable abelian surfaces are likewise represented by torsion cosets in the moduli space of stable abelian surfaces.

The detection of very high-energy (TeV) gamma rays from numerous Galactic sources has significantly advanced our understanding of the diffuse Galactic gamma-ray emission spectrum. This review examines the TeV observations of the Galactic center region, focusing on the unresolved emission from the central source and the TeV counterparts of the Fermi-LAT cataloged sources.

This study examines the geometric characteristics of diffusion models governed by nonlocal boundary conditions. We demonstrate that the specific shape of the domain influences the model's behavior, and we derive an explicit formula for the principal eigenvalue of the associated operator.

We present a novel method for classifying compact stellar systems (CSSs) using their color distributions. This approach employs a convolutional neural network (CNN) trained on simulated images of CSSs, which were generated using the GENEVA stellar population synthesis code. The simulations utilized the MILES stellar library and incorporated various physical parameters, including metallicity, age, and the initial mass function (IMF). The network was trained on 1,000 simulated images and validated against a test set of 1,000 images. The results demonstrate that the CNN successfully classifies simulated CSSs with an accuracy of 99.9%. Furthermore, the model effectively distinguishes between simulated globular clusters (GCs) and globular cluster-like systems (GC-like systems) with 99.8% accuracy. The study also reveals that the blue and red color bands provide the most significant information for classification. Finally, the method was applied to classify real CSSs using the Hubble Space Telescope's WFC3/IR instrument, achieving a classification accuracy of 99.7%.

Simulations are frequently employed to evaluate Recommender Systems (RS) and their components, offering a valuable means to enhance the development process. This paper introduces a simulation framework for RS that leverages the open-source Python package `simrs`. The tool enables the modeling of user-item interaction patterns, the execution of experiments, and the assessment of various recommender algorithms.

This study introduces a novel approach to hypothesis testing for distributions characterized by infinite mean or variance, utilizing truncated sample means. The proposed method is demonstrated through its application to the Cauchy distribution, specifically for testing the location parameter.

This study introduces a new approach to EEG-based Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCI) that leverages the strengths of both Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs). While CNNs excel at capturing spatial features, they struggle with temporal dependencies, a limitation that RNNs are designed to overcome. To address this, we propose a hybrid architecture that integrates the spatial processing capabilities of CNNs with the sequential modeling strengths of RNNs. Our method utilizes a hybrid CNN-LSTM model to extract spatial features from raw EEG signals and subsequently employs a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network to model the temporal dynamics of these features. We evaluated this framework on a public dataset containing 100 trials of 10-class motor imagery tasks. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed hybrid model outperforms standalone CNNs and RNNs, achieving an average accuracy of 96.1%.

This study examines the $AdS/CFT$ correspondence concerning a massive scalar field within a noncommutative space, specifically focusing on the $AdS_5$ background. We derive the holographic dual of the noncommutative scalar field theory and analyze the resulting two-point correlation function. Furthermore, we investigate the impact of noncommutativity on the thermal behavior of the dual field theory.

This study examines the application of Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) to model acceptance choices for kidney transplants. We introduce a novel MDP formulation that integrates patient-incompatibility as a dynamic state variable, enabling the analysis of how patient and donor attributes influence acceptance decisions. Furthermore, we present a new algorithm capable of solving this specific MDP model.

This study examines the hidden state structures of both Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. We demonstrate that the HMM's inherent state topology is isomorphic to a complete graph, whereas the LSTM's structure corresponds to a complete bipartite graph. Furthermore, we establish that the transition dynamics within an HMM are equivalent to a random walk on a complete graph, while those in an LSTM align with a random walk on a complete bipartite graph. These findings offer a novel perspective on the LSTM's architecture and its capacity to model temporal dependencies.

This study examines weighted composition operators acting on weighted Bergman spaces. We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for such an operator to be compact or to belong to the Schatten class, utilizing the essential norm of the operator's Hankel counterpart. Furthermore, we derive sufficient conditions for the operator to be nilpotent.

This study evaluates the efficacy of various compression techniques for text classification, specifically examining quantization, pruning, and knowledge distillation. We assess these methods across three datasets—IMDB, AG News, and MNLI—using four distinct models: BERT, RoBERTa, DistilBERT, and ALBERT. Our findings indicate that ALBERT quantization provides the optimal balance between model size and performance. Additionally, we observe that pruning yields the most significant performance degradation, whereas knowledge distillation delivers the most substantial improvements.

The field of high-energy physics (HEP) is currently undergoing a transformation driven by the unprecedented scale of data generated by the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). This shift has necessitated a new approach to data analysis, one that relies on sophisticated software tools and frameworks. To meet these demands, HEP is increasingly adopting software engineering practices, such as continuous integration, automated testing, and version control. This paper outlines the current landscape of software development within HEP and proposes the concept of "computing science" as a new role to bridge the gap between data scientists and software engineers. This role is designed to enhance the creation and deployment of tools for data analysis, visualization, and simulation. Furthermore, the text highlights the importance of open-source software in HEP, emphasizing the need for greater collaboration between the HEP community and the broader software engineering sector.

We introduce generalized Howe curves, defined as decomposed Richelot curves that possess a specific set of ramification points. Furthermore, we establish the explicit equations for their associated generalized Howe elliptic curves, which are Jacobian varieties formed by decomposed Richelot isogenies.

This paper introduces a novel approach for analyzing errors in matrix approximation by leveraging invariant matrix theory. We demonstrate that the discrepancy between an approximated matrix and its original counterpart can be characterized as a scaled projection onto a specific subspace. This framework enables the derivation of tight, closed-form error bounds for various matrix norms, which are subsequently applied to assess the accuracy of the Nyström method for low-rank matrix approximation.

This study examines the Wikipedia article structure by analyzing the raw wikitext markup and comparing it against rendered HTML. We evaluate the divergence between these two formats, specifically focusing on how the HTML parser interprets wikitext. Our findings indicate that while wikitext and HTML share a high degree of similarity, the HTML parser does not fully adhere to the specification, leading to discrepancies. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the parser's behavior is influenced by the specific wikitext syntax employed.

The polar domains found in twisted bilayers offer a promising avenue for investigating topological physics. We demonstrate that the polar domains within twisted bilayer hexagonal crystals can be described using a topological framework. Specifically, we establish a correspondence between the polar domains and the edge states of a corresponding topological insulator. Furthermore, we show that the polar domains in twisted bilayers can be manipulated by adjusting the twist angle, which allows for the creation of domain walls hosting topological states.

This study examines light propagation in a non-flat universe, demonstrating that the resulting effects differ from those in flat cosmologies. We propose a method to quantify these effects and suggest that they could be observable in the near future.

This study investigates the movement of colloids within a liquid crystal situated between a wavy wall and a flat plate. The wavy wall features alternating hills and valleys, creating a periodic potential that influences particle paths. We demonstrate that, under specific conditions, this configuration can generate either trapping or repulsion effects. Furthermore, we examine the impact of varying the liquid crystal's elastic constants on these trajectories.

This study examines the influence of tidal forces on the elongation of a spherical asteroid, modeled as a homogeneous, isotropic, linear elastic body, within the restricted three-body framework. The analysis focuses on the asteroid's behavior outside the Roche limit, where it remains intact. The findings indicate that elongation increases as the asteroid moves further from the Roche limit and that the tidal effects are more pronounced in elongated asteroids compared to spherical ones. Additionally, the research demonstrates that the asteroid's elongation is highly sensitive to the specific values of its elastic constants.

The synergy of machine learning (ML) and quantum computing (QC) offers significant potential for advancing molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, particularly in capturing rare conformational transitions. This study introduces a quantum-inspired framework that integrates ML and QC to enhance MD simulations. The approach employs a quantum-inspired algorithm to construct a Markov state model (MSM) from MD trajectories, enabling the prediction of rare events. Furthermore, the framework utilizes a quantum-inspired algorithm to estimate the free energy landscape of the system. The efficacy of this method is demonstrated through its application to the alanine dipeptide, a standard benchmark in MD simulations.

We introduce MAPPIES, a new Monte-Carlo code designed to simulate polarisation in X-ray and gamma-ray emissions from the inverse Compton scattering of photons off relativistic electrons. This tool is intended to support the analysis of polarisation data from upcoming missions, such as the proposed eXTP. The software is publicly accessible at https://github.com/astro-umh/MAPPIES.

This study examines the impact of open water on the seasonal development of sea-ice thickness categories. We introduce a novel approach to the sea-ice thickness distribution (SID) model that incorporates open water dynamics, which are typically omitted in standard formulations. This method utilizes a simplified representation of the ocean-ice-atmosphere system to derive a time-varying, state-dependent threshold for open water occurrence. We demonstrate that the resulting SID model is a piecewise ordinary differential equation (ODE) system, which is solved numerically. Our analysis reveals that open water significantly alters the seasonal evolution of the SID, particularly in the Arctic region. Furthermore, we show that the SID model is highly sensitive to the parameters of the coupled ocean-ice-atmosphere system.

This paper examines two specific families of Hermitian curve covers, denoted as $\mathcal{X}_{a,b,n,s}$ and $\mathcal{Y}_{n,s}$. We demonstrate that these two families are distinct, and we establish that every curve within the $\mathcal{X}_{a,b,n,s}$ series is isomorphic to a corresponding curve in the $\mathcal{Y}_{n,s}$ series.

The authors provide a detailed description of the dataset's structure and content, along with a comparative analysis of the acoustic characteristics between the original and expanded versions. Graph learning has proven highly effective across diverse domains, including social networks, e-commerce, knowledge graphs, and biological networks. However, the majority of existing research has primarily focused on social and e-commerce contexts. This paper provides a comprehensive review of graph learning methodologies applied to knowledge graphs and biological networks. We begin by outlining the fundamental concepts of graph learning, followed by an examination of knowledge graphs and biological networks, along with their specific characteristics. Subsequently, we categorize and analyze graph learning techniques tailored to these two fields, highlighting their unique challenges and opportunities. Finally, we conclude with a discussion on future research directions.

This study introduces a new 3D guidance system for retinal surgery that utilizes a specialized projection mechanism to map the 3D coordinates of a handheld probe onto the patient's retina. By leveraging the probe's position and orientation alongside the probe's light pattern, the system creates a 3D visual aid for the surgeon. The proposed approach is validated through a simulation of a probe navigating a retinal hole, demonstrating the system's ability to accurately track the probe's 3D location.

The FIDO2 standard is a key driver in the transition away from password-based authentication. This paper introduces a novel, privacy-centric approach to FIDO2 that leverages a Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) to enhance the security of the credential management system. By relocating the credential store to the TEE, the proposed method ensures that sensitive data remains inaccessible to the relying party, the authenticator, and the FIDO2 server. This architecture is designed to safeguard user privacy and mitigate the risks of credential theft.
This study demonstrates that the recently proposed Weyl-Wigner framework for quantum information processing fails to adequately address the quantum mechanics of qubits.

This paper introduces a novel video interface designed to enhance user control over playback by incorporating a timeline and a progress bar. We conducted a user study to assess how these elements influence the sense of control users feel, alongside their impact on enjoyment and engagement. The findings indicate that the progress bar significantly boosts the perception of control, whereas the timeline has a more modest effect. Furthermore, the study reveals that users' sense of control positively correlates with enjoyment and engagement, suggesting that interface features which foster this sense of control can lead to higher enjoyment and greater engagement.
This paper demonstrates that the $\pi$-calculus possesses greater expressive power than reactive Turing machines regarding the specification of behaviors that cannot be executed in finite time.

We introduce a newly designed Gray code for ordered trees that transitions between consecutive encodings by performing exactly one elementary rotation. This code is constructed using a specific recursive approach, and we provide an efficient algorithm to generate the next tree in the sequence based on the current tree and its depth.

This study introduces a time-discontinuous prismatic space-time (D-PST) method designed to address the challenges of free-surface flow simulations. The approach utilizes a prismatic space-time framework, which effectively eliminates the need for finite elements to intersect the free surface. The method's accuracy is validated through comparisons with existing literature, and its performance is further assessed using a series of test cases that evaluate both its stability and precision.

This paper examines circular flows in signed graphs, specifically focusing on the relationship between circular $r_k$-flows and modulo $k$-orientations. We demonstrate that a signed graph admits a circular $r_k$-flow if and only if it possesses a modulo $k$-orientation that respects the graph's negative edge signs. Additionally, we establish that the flow polytope of a signed graph is equivalent to the base polyhedron of its corresponding modulo $k$-orientation.

We present a deterministic algorithm for the Modular Subset Sum problem that runs in $O(n^2)$ time, improving upon the prior best-known bound of $O(n^3)$ by Bringmann and Narayanan. This approach adapts Bringmann and Narayanan's randomized method, which relies on the Schwartz-Zippel lemma, by replacing it with a deterministic strategy that utilizes the Chinese Remainder Theorem.

We analyzed the light curves of 1,000 stars from the TSS and the Taurus Planetary Nebula Survey (TPNS) to determine the variability of M dwarf stars in the Taurus molecular cloud, using a dataset of 1,000 stars from the Taurus Spectroscopic Survey (TSS) and the Taurus Planetary Nebula Survey (TPNS). The study investigates the motility of hemocytes, which are immune cells in the hemolymph of the fruit fly *Drosophila melanogaster*. These cells move through a three-dimensional environment, and their behavior is analyzed using a stochastic model that incorporates both active and passive forces. The active forces are modeled as a combination of a constant and a time-varying component, while the passive forces are represented by a time-dependent Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process. The model's parameters are estimated using a Bayesian framework, and the results are validated against experimental data. The study also explores the effects of various mutations on hemocyte motility, including the LanB1 and SCAR mutants, which exhibit reduced motility, and the *ptc* mutant, which exhibits increased motility. The study concludes that the proposed model provides a good fit to the experimental data and can be used to study the effects of various mutations on hemocyte motility.

This study introduces c-siam, a new architecture designed to extract linguistic information from speech data. c-siam builds upon siam, a prior model that utilizes a Siamese structure to learn representations from pairs of utterances. The primary advancement in c-siam is the integration of a contrastive loss function, which explicitly guides the model to distinguish between utterances containing different words. This approach yields superior performance compared to siam and other state-of-the-art methods across various tasks, including phoneme classification, phoneme recognition, and phoneme sequence prediction.

This study addresses the stabilization of linear systems influenced by hidden Markov chains, where the system dynamics are only partially observable. We introduce a novel adaptive control strategy that leverages the known system model to achieve almost sure stabilization. The approach utilizes a certainty equivalence principle, where the unknown Markov chain states are estimated using a maximum likelihood method. Furthermore, we establish the almost sure stability of the resulting closed-loop system.

This paper introduces BTAI, a novel framework for autonomous driving that integrates the BTAI and AIT methods. BTAI demonstrates superior performance compared to both predecessors, achieving a 20% reduction in task completion time and a 10% increase in success rates.

This study derives the Korteveg-de Vries (KdV) equation for the longitudinal fluctuations of the quark gluon plasma (QGP) within the framework of the Bjorken flow. The derivation relies on the hydrodynamic equations of the QGP, which are established using an equation of state (EoS) that incorporates the medium's shear viscosity. The resulting QGP KdV equation is subsequently compared with the standard KdV equation for the longitudinal fluctuations of a cold plasma.

This paper demonstrates that the space of linearly Eberlein-Grothendieck continuous real-valued functions on a compact space is characterized as such if and only if the compact space is a countable union of compact metrizable subspaces.

This paper introduces a novel approach to the isochronicity problem, which involves determining the conditions under which a Hamiltonian system exhibits purely imaginary eigenvalues. We demonstrate that the Taylor coefficients of the Hamiltonian function can be expressed as linear combinations of isochronic coefficients, which are defined as the Taylor coefficients of the corresponding generating function. This method is applied to analyze the isochronicity of a specific class of polynomial Hamiltonians, including the quadratic and cubic cases.

The Lorenz system is a well-known example of a chaotic attractor. Periodic orbits within this system are categorized by their period lengths, which are determined by the number of lobes the trajectory traverses. This paper demonstrates that the number of such orbits with a specific period $k$ is given by the $k$-th Fibonacci number.

This paper examines the application of Malliavin calculus to the derivatives of log-likelihood in a statistical framework where the likelihood function is expressed as a functional of a Gaussian process. We demonstrate that the derivatives of the log-likelihood can be represented as a sum of chaos components, which facilitates the derivation of a Poincaré inequality. This inequality is instrumental in establishing an upper bound for the variance of these log-likelihood derivatives.

We examine the spectrum of Laplacians defined on the unit tangent bundle of a compact, locally symmetric space of rank one. This spectrum is linked to the spectrum of Casimir operators within the metaplectic cover of the complexified real Lie algebra of the space's isometry group. We demonstrate that the critical exponents corresponding to these representations correspond to the eigenvalues of the Laplacian. Furthermore, we establish that the critical exponents for irreducible representations are non-degenerate. Additionally, we derive a formula for the first-order variation of the Laplacian's eigenvalues under Teichmüller deformations, showing that these variations are governed by the critical exponents of the underlying representations.

This paper introduces the autoregressive Fourier transform (ARFT), a technique designed to enhance the predictive performance of time-series models by leveraging the inherent smoothness of their Fourier representations. We demonstrate that ARFT can be seamlessly integrated into existing architectures, such as the Transformer, without necessitating any modifications to their internal structure. Empirical results indicate that ARFT consistently improves prediction accuracy across various time-series forecasting tasks.

This study examines the compatibility of various cosmological models with observational data by analyzing cosmic parameters such as energy density, the equation of state, and the deceleration parameter. The investigation covers both dark energy and dark matter scenarios, including the $\Lambda$CDM model, the Holographic Dark Energy (HDE) model, the Generalized Chaplygin Gas (GCG) model, and the Generalized Proca (GP) model. The results indicate that the HDE and GP models align well with observational data, whereas the GCG model exhibits a significant discrepancy.

This study addresses the resource allocation for service function chains (SFCs) within multi-access edge computing (MEC) environments. The objective is to minimize the total service latency by optimizing the placement and scheduling of SFCs across distributed MEC nodes. The problem is decomposed into two distinct subproblems: SFC placement and SFC scheduling. To address SFC placement, we introduce a novel algorithm grounded in the concept of a minimum spanning tree (MST). For the scheduling task, we develop a new method utilizing a bipartite graph. The proposed algorithm is evaluated against existing approaches, demonstrating superior performance in reducing service latency.

We investigate the renormalization group flow of a two-dimensional Dirac fermion system coupled to a U(1) gauge field within a disordered environment. By employing a one-loop approximation, we derive the beta functions for the coupling constants and analyze their fixed points. Our findings indicate that fixed points are generally unstable, except in the limit of zero disorder strength. Furthermore, we examine the phase diagram resulting from varying the coupling constants and disorder strength.

We examine a QCD-like framework featuring a scalar sector that may account for dark matter. This model is characterized by a scalar potential that is non-trivially renormalizable, and we analyze its phenomenology within the context of the Standard Model.

The spin dynamics of Na$_{4-\delta}$NiTeO$_{6}$, a triangular-lattice system, were investigated using inelastic neutron scattering. The study reveals that the crystalline electric field significantly reduces the Ni$^{2+}$ spin moment from the expected 1 $\mu_{\rm B}$ to 0.6 $\mu_{\rm B}$, thereby weakening the antiferromagnetic correlations. Furthermore, the spin-wave dispersion is found to be highly anisotropic, with the out-of-plane mode being markedly softer than the in-plane mode.

In large-scale distributed systems like the Internet of Things, trust plays a pivotal role in decision-making. This paper introduces a novel framework for modeling trust in such environments, utilizing a Bayesian network to represent the trust relationships among various entities. We outline a methodology for constructing this network and demonstrate its application through a case study involving a smart home.

Cubic splines are widely utilized in various fields, including computer graphics, geostatistics, and data interpolation. However, in specific applications, it is crucial to maintain data monotonicity, which necessitates the use of monotone cubic splines. This paper introduces a novel method for constructing such splines, which is both straightforward and computationally efficient. The approach is founded on a specific property of the second derivative of the spline, which is defined as a piecewise linear function. The method's efficacy is demonstrated through numerical examples.

This study examines the transition between de Sitter and anti-de Sitter geometries within the framework of exact black bounces. We demonstrate that while de Sitter configurations smoothly evolve into one another, anti-de Sitter transitions are discontinuous. Furthermore, we analyze the thermodynamic properties of these black bounces, specifically focusing on the Hawking temperature and entropy.

This paper introduces a new dataset designed for the automatic transcription of audio content featuring diverse languages, musical instruments, and sound effects. We outline the specific challenges encountered during the manual annotation process and the subsequent curation of the dataset. Additionally, we present a new end-to-end model for audio-to-text conversion that leverages a pre-trained speech recognition system. Experimental results indicate that this approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on our dataset.

The stability of diversity in both biochemical and ecological systems is fundamentally linked to fluctuations in species population levels. While the mean abundances of these populations are typically regulated by interactions among species, their fluctuations are primarily driven by stochastic birth and death events. This study examines the relationship between these two factors by analyzing a stochastic model of a food web. We demonstrate that fluctuations in population numbers are governed by a covariance matrix, which is determined by the network's topology and the interaction strengths between species. Furthermore, we show that the stability of diversity is directly connected to the magnitude of these fluctuations.

This study examines the evolution of a network following the removal of a single node, specifically focusing on the resulting avalanche of cascading failures. We demonstrate that the avalanche size is governed by a power law with respect to the initial node's degree, where the exponent depends on the network's dimensionality. Furthermore, we derive an analytical formula for the total number of avalanches occurring throughout the fragmentation process.

While discourse comprehension is a critical component of human communication, constructing models capable of holistic understanding remains difficult due to the scarcity of large-scale datasets. This paper introduces a new dataset comprising 1,000 articles from the New York Times, annotated with 1,000 corresponding summaries. We present a new model that leverages the article's full text to generate these holistic summaries. Our approach utilizes a pre-trained language model, fine-tuned on the article's content, to produce these outputs. Our results demonstrate that our model significantly outperforms existing baselines, achieving a 1,000-point improvement in ROUGE-L scores.

This paper introduces a novel implementation of Perfectly Matched Layers (PML) for solving seismological problems, utilizing the PML's inherent flexibility to apply the technique selectively to specific components of the wave field. This selective approach allows for a significant reduction in computational resources, achieving savings of up to 90% in certain scenarios.

The rapid proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has created a significant demand for enhanced traffic management and Quality of Service (QoS) within IoT networks. To address this, Software-Defined Networking (SDN) offers a centralized control plane that enables dynamic traffic management and QoS assurance. This paper introduces a novel, SDN-driven framework designed to optimize IoT traffic management and QoS delivery. The proposed solution leverages a centralized controller to monitor network conditions and adjust traffic flows accordingly, while simultaneously employing a machine learning algorithm to predict traffic patterns and proactively manage congestion. The framework's efficacy is evaluated through simulations, demonstrating its ability to reduce latency and packet loss, thereby ensuring superior QoS for IoT applications.

This study investigates the impact of planetary orbits on the structure of protoplanetary disks. We examine the formation of a gap in a disk surrounding a planet on a highly inclined orbit, specifically one with an inclination of 30° and an eccentricity of 0.5. Our findings indicate that the planet's orbital shape significantly influences disk morphology. Specifically, the gap's width and depth are primarily dictated by the planet's pericenter distance, while the disk's outer edge is determined by the planet's apocenter distance.

This study examines the application of symmetric positive definite (SPD) matrices within the context of the matrix manifold. We introduce a novel model utilizing a specific type of matrix exponential, which is trained on the MNIST dataset. Our findings indicate that this model performs comparably to those based on Euclidean and hyperbolic spaces, while also demonstrating superior efficiency in terms of computational time.
